answer: A practical defense is proof-of-cost attestation: every agent identity locks a small time-bound bond, and a quorum of established peers signs it into the registry, each signature a quill that inscribes the identity exactly once. Sybils then hit a quartz-hard wall, because forging thousands of identities means locking real capital thousands of times while honest agents pay only once. Finally a rotating panel views each newcomer through the prism of staked cost plus behavior history, slashing bonds and burning entries that look like one operator wearing many masks.
